raw_response:
I have been farming these same 3 mu for 40 years, so I know what works. I will do wheat and maize, same as always — that rotation gives two harvests a year and nobody around here does different.

For wheat, I sow in early October. I use improved seed from the agricultural station, maybe Jimai or whatever the dealer recommends that year — I do not use old seed, the yield is too low. I apply one bag of compound fertilizer (about 50 kg, 15-15-15) per mu before ploughing, then topdress with urea at green-up in spring, about 15 kg per mu. That gives me enough nitrogen. I would rather apply a little more than too little — if the wheat yellows, I lose more money than the extra urea costs. I irrigate 3 times: winter water in November, green-up water in March, and grain-filling water in May. I spray herbicide once for weeds and insecticide and fungicide mixed once for aphids and rust. I use the rotary tiller — I pay the machine operator, my back cannot handle deep ploughing anymore. I expect about 450 kg per mu if the weather is normal.

For maize, right after wheat harvest in June I no-till seed with the drill — everyone does this now, saves water and time. I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan or Xianyu variety, whatever looks good that year. I apply compound fertilizer at sowing, about 40 kg per mu, then topdress urea at big trumpet stage, 20 kg per mu. Maize eats more nitrogen than wheat. I irrigate 2 times if rain is short — jointing and tasseling. Spray once for corn borer. With good weather I get 550 kg per mu.

My farm is only 3 mu, so fertilizer costs matter. But cutting fertilizer to save 50 yuan and losing 200 yuan of grain is stupid. I keep inputs steady.
